Marissa / team,

Thanks for flagging — I reviewed the redlines and Velotech's questions. High-level recommendations below; attached is a short comment file with suggested clause text (DPA_Irene_comments_20260302.pdf).

1) Lawful-hold / regulatory requests
- Acceptable to include a lawful-hold exception, but must require: (a) written notice from Controller (Velotech) describing legal basis, scope, and estimated duration; (b) Controller to sign a short addendum or confirm via DocuSign; (c) Redwood to implement retention only as narrowly necessary and notify Controller of the exact data elements retained.
- Add an obligation on Controller to respond to Redwood queries within 5 business days to confirm scope.

2) Retention limits
- Maintain proposed 90-day default for request/trace logs.
- Allow aggregated/instrumentation metrics retention up to 2 years, provided they are pseudonymized.

3) SCCs and Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA)
- We should adopt the EU Commission SCCs. Insert a Transfer Impact Addendum reference: Controller must provide any country-specific legal guidance and complete a TIA prior to initial transfer to a restricted jurisdiction.
- Add a short sentence stating Redwood will execute the SCCs as Processor and maintain a public subprocessor list; updates to subprocessor list to be provided at least 30 days in advance.

4) Subprocessor access / debugging
- For engineering/bug investigation we can allow limited access by Redwood personnel under role-based access and written NDA; include requirement for audit logs and KMS-approved key handling.

5) Audit rights / certifications
- Limit Controller audit rights to one SOC/ISO review per 12 months, with redacted reports acceptable; allow evidence bundle rather than on-site for SaaS deployments.

I attached specific suggested language. Once Marissa consolidates, we can produce an "Agree/Decline" matrix for Velotech and propose DocuSign.
